title: The Czech September notice leaves the repo rate and corridor in place
summary: On September 17 the CNB announced no change in the two-week repo rate of 3.75%, the discount rate of 2.75% or the Lombard rate of 4.75%. The width and central point of the corridor therefore stayed the same. The release itself does not express a preference for the next decision.

The information available at 14:30 Prague time was the identity and level of the three unchanged instruments. A daily return would mix this rate confirmation with information released at the later press conference. For a decision-only observation use trades after the notice but before that second release, and measure the unexpected component against pricing recorded beforehand.

questions.question: Was the rate confirmation a surprise at the closest maturity?
questions.detail: Compare the pre-announcement implied September setting, adjusted for meeting-day weighting, with the actual 3.75% repo rate.

questions.question: Was forward-rate repricing already visible before 15:00?
questions.detail: Use timestamped subsequent-meeting contracts to compare pre-release pricing with quotes in the thirty minutes after the decision. Record any additional response later separately.

questions.question: Did any currency response differ from the regional move?
questions.detail: Compare intraday koruna returns with regional currencies and euro interest rates. A simultaneous common influence could affect local markets in the same short window.
